input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator condition is inverted, changing the existing help output for options with secondary spellings.
- rationale: For a boolean option declared as `--foo/--no-foo`, `any_prefix_is_slash` is false, so this now renders `--foo; --no-foo` instead of `--foo / --no-foo`. Slash-prefixed option pairs receive the opposite incorrect separator. Since `get_help_record` delegates to this method, existing command help output changes.
critique: The finding describes the same inverted separator condition on any_prefix_is_slash. Under it, `--foo/--no-foo` renders with '; ' and slash-prefixed options get ' / '. This is the same mechanism and the same failure as the label.
